big_case.notes: Routine last-minute capital stay application arising from a successive state postconviction denial; presents a recurring, repeatedly rejected Woodard clemency challenge with no circuit split, no amicus participation, no response call from the Court, and a summary unsigned denial without noted dissent.

leakage.notes: Forward prediction placed on 2026-11-04T01:40:43Z, one day before the November 5, 2026 disposition. Retrieval log shows only pre-resolution lookups: Ohio Adult Parole Authority v. Woodard, 523 U.S. 272 (1998) on CourtListener (retrieved_doc_date 1998-03-25) and corpus queries for 26A623, 26-6013, and prior capital stay applications.

central_claims.basis: On November 5, 2026, the docket records: 'Application (26A623) for a stay of execution of sentence of death, submitted to Justice Thomas, and by him referred to the Court, is denied.' Companion cert petition No. 26-6013 was denied the same day.
central_claims.claim: Justice Thomas will refer Application 26A623 to the full Court, and the Court will deny the stay application in an unsigned, unreasoned order on or before November 5, 2026, alongside denial of certiorari in No. 26-6013.

central_claims.basis: outcome.json records interim_signals.response_requested = false and amicus_briefs = 0; snapshot 2026-11-05.json shows Florida filed its response voluntarily on November 2 and Guardado replied on November 3 without a Court order requesting a response.
central_claims.claim: The State of Florida will file a brief in opposition prior to disposition, most likely voluntarily without a formal Court-ordered call for response, and no amicus briefs will be filed.

central_claims.basis: outcome.json records votes: [], noted_dissent_from_denial: null, and writing_roles: null; the November 5, 2026 order carries no separate writings or noted dissents.
central_claims.claim: The denial order will issue with no separate opinions and no publicly recorded dissents from any Justice.

central_claims.basis: The Court denied the application in a single-sentence unsigned order without stating a doctrinal rationale.
central_claims.claim: Under Nken v. Holder and Hill v. McDonough, the application fails to show a reasonable probability of certiorari or reversal because neither Chief Justice Rehnquist's plurality nor Justice O'Connor's concurrence in Woodard supports invalidating a state clemency system based on historical grant statistics or gubernatorial policy statements.
